title: Files: formats, failures, and explicit saving
goal: Separate an input file, an output artifact and a saved project file. Verify each transition separately.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–2: expressions, comparisons, types, references, and checked cin.
Follow the prerequisite links: cpp.multifile-build, cpp.streams-state. New constructs are introduced before the assignment.

sections.title: A file as a resource
paragraphs: Within one run the program writes 73 to sample.txt, closes the stream and opens a reader. Predict stdout first, then check the file’s contents itself.

ifstream from <fstream> reads a file; ofstream writes one. Construction associates the stream with a path, and destruction closes the resource. Check opening through bool(stream). RAII cleanup is useful, but successful opening does not guarantee every later operation succeeds.
A regular ofstream may truncate an existing file. Do not open an input file for writing before validating its data. The lab writes a separate report.txt and preserves records.txt.

sections.title: Write and read within one run
paragraphs: Trace what appears after closing output and what the reader extracts from sample.txt.

reveal.title: Reveal output and trace execution
paragraphs: Both stdout and sample.txt contain 73 and a newline. This verifies writing and reading within one run.

sections.title: The format is an interface
paragraphs: A text format defines encoding, delimiters, field counts, and bounds. The lab records.txt contains one integer in -1000…1000 per line, at most 100 lines of 200 bytes. An empty file is valid; a blank line is malformed.

Parse each line using a local istringstream and reject trailing data. Do not save a struct by dumping its memory: padding, type sizes, and byte order may differ. A textual contract is easier to verify manually and with two compilers.
An empty records.txt file is valid, but a blank line is one malformed record. The line delimiter and value bounds are part of the format contract.

sections.title: Read and write failures
paragraphs: A missing file produces missing; a malformed record produces invalid. Do not treat every stopped getline as normal completion: check bad and unexpected failure without eof. A partial import must not generate a successful final report.

After writing, call close and check the stream: flushing can fail late. The lab distinguishes write-error from invalid. This does not promise atomic replacement after a crash; that needs a separate storage strategy.
Distinguish an absent records.txt, a bad record inside it and a report.txt write failure. The program reports separate outcomes and only opens the report after a successful import.

sections.title: The Nexus virtual filesystem
paragraphs: A program sees relative files supplied with its request. Absolute paths, .., and system directories are unavailable. Every run receives a fresh runtime filesystem; a previous run’s file does not appear automatically in the next. stdin is not a substitute for testing file input.

Limits are 128 files, 512 KiB per file, 2 MiB for input and runtime files, and 2 MiB of writes per run. Exceeding them is a provider limitation distinct from an algorithm defect. Do not raise quotas to bypass an exercise.
The second example gets its text from input.txt in the request files, not stdin. Open the input-file list to check what was read.

sections.title: A file supplied from the project VFS
paragraphs: Open input.txt and identify where the printed line came from.

sections.title: An artifact and a personal project
paragraphs: The result panel lists new or changed runtime files. Downloading saves a separate copy. Saving text results transfers them into the VFS only through an explicit action and when no conflicting edits exist. A program cannot silently replace source code.

A binary result downloads as bytes rather than becoming an editor text file. A conflict preserves the project source. For another run, explicitly save a permitted text file, then rerun the reader and compare contents.
If report.txt appears among the run results, inspect its bytes first. Save it to the project explicitly only when you want it available for another run.

sections.title: Roundtrip evidence
paragraphs: Separately test a missing file, a valid import, malformed data, export, and report.txt contents. Then confirm saving into the project and a fresh run. Reading within the same run does not establish that final step.

Use synthetic data only; do not put keys or personal work into evidence. Next, a linked list demonstrates node-resource management, while the final project combines records, commands, tests, and file formats.
Compare a missing file, an empty file and a file containing a newline. Separately verify that invalid did not create a new report.txt.

sections.title: Now try your own task
paragraphs: Build a report for a different format: one integer per line in the input file. Print the operation status and put report data in a separate artifact.
Write expected stdout and report.txt for a file with lines 2, −1 and 4. Record what should happen if the second line is changed to bad.

feedback: Correct. The reader extracts 73 from the file just written.

options: No; inspect the artifact and explicitly save it

selfcheck.feedback: Write output to a separate path after validating input.

Will a runtime file automatically appear in the next run?
options: No; explicit acceptance into the project is needed

selfcheck.prompt: What is needed to accept this lab?
options: Source, actual results, original tests, and a contract explanation
selfcheck.feedback: A progress flag is not evidence of independent mastery.

selfcheck.prompt: Why does exported alone fail to prove report.txt is saved in the project? How can you check bytes and availability in a fresh run separately?
selfcheck.feedback: For the empty-file test, keep records.txt in the bundle with zero bytes. For missing, remove it only from a separate test copy.

practice.title: Import records.txt and produce report.txt
practice.task: Read at most 100 lines of up to 200 bytes from records.txt, exactly one integer in −1000 through 1000 per line. An empty file is valid; a blank line is invalid. On success, write the count and sum separated by a space and followed by a newline to report.txt, then print exported. A missing file gives missing, malformed input gives invalid and a write failure gives write-error. Check the artifact separately.
criteria: Verify the status and artifact bytes separately. On success expect exported and 3 5 followed by a newline in the file. Test missing input and a malformed record.
Creating a runtime file and saving it into a personal project are separate actions.
Do not open the input with ofstream before validation. Do not assume ambient runtime persistence between runs.
Add two cases of your own, including a rejection if the interface allows one. Explain one boundary result.
Keep the source, exact input and observed output.
practice.hint: For the empty-file test, keep records.txt in the bundle with zero bytes. For missing, remove it only from a separate test copy.

steps.action: Write expected stdout and report.txt for a file with lines 2, −1 and 4. Record what should happen if the second line is changed to bad.
Parse one line at a time. Open report.txt only after validating all records and check the stream after close.
Verify the status and artifact bytes separately. On success expect exported and 3 5 followed by a newline in the file. Test missing input and a malformed record.
